cohort: This study included 356 nulliparous pregnant women whose vaginal swabs were collected late in the third trimester, and their infants whose oral swabs were examined.
finding: The study found that 22% of women were positive for vaginal Candida spp., but only 25% of mother/infant dyads showed C. albicans co-colonisation, suggesting non-maternal sources are likely involved in determining infant oral colonisation status.
